To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the success rate of clinical lipid control in patients with coronary disease was low after 9 months of follow-up after PCI.
despite the improvement in the lipid profile of patients, dyslipidemia remained in a considerable proportion.
the prevalence of patients having dyslipidemia was 80.5%, 65.6% and 63.1% for low total cholesterol, low LDL-C and non HDL-C levels, respectively, after 9 months of follow-up.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the clinical lipid control success rate before and after percutaneous intervention in Iran.
the clinical lipid control success rate in patients who underwent PCI.
the clinical control of lipids after percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current treatment of dyslipidemia is not satisfactory and further researches are needed.
lipid control in patients after PCI is still a challenge.
the success rate of dyslipidemia control after percutaneous intervention is still not satisfactory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
although by current treatments, lipid control has significantly increased, dyslipidemia persists in a considerable proportion.
the prevalence of high serum TC, LDL-C, and non-HDL- C has significantly increased after PCI, but a considerable number of patients still had dyslipidemia.
although the prevalence of patients having low TC, LDL, and non-HDL increased significantly during follow up, dyslipidemia still persisted in a considerable number of patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
despite lipid-lowering therapy, the lipid control rate was not high in patients with coronary atherosclerosis.
lipid control in patients with CAD is a challenge and further studies are needed to improve the treatment strategies in this group of patients.
dyslipidemia remains a major risk factor for coronary artery disease.
